steps.tx: An **osteosarcoma** represents the most common primary malignant bone neoplasm in children and young adolescents, displaying a peak incidence between ten and twenty years of age. A second smaller incidence peak occurs in adults over sixty, frequently arising secondary to Paget disease of bone or prior irradiation. The tumour characteristically originates in the metaphysis of rapidly growing long bones around the knee.
steps.say: Osteosarcoma is the commonest primary malignant bone cancer in children and teenagers, peaking between ten and twenty years. A second peak happens in elderly patients with Paget disease. It arises in rapidly growing metaphyses around the knee, specifically the lower femur and upper tibia.

vis.caption: Radiographic hallmarks of osteosarcoma including cortical erosion and periosteal elevation.

steps.tx: The definitive histopathological criterion defining osteosarcoma is the direct production of unmineralized bone matrix, or **malignant osteoid**, by pleomorphic mesenchymal stromal cells. The neoplastic cells display hyperchromatic, atypical nuclei with frequent mitotic figures. The World Health Organization categorizes conventional osteosarcoma into osteoblastic, chondroblastic, and fibroblastic subtypes based on the dominant extracellular matrix produced, although all share identical clinical staging and prognosis.
steps.say: The hallmark of osteosarcoma is that malignant stromal cells directly manufacture osteoid or immature bone. The malignant spindle cells have bizarre, hyperchromatic nuclei with atypical mitoses. Whether the tumor matrix is predominantly bone, cartilage, or fibrous tissue, all conventional subtypes follow the same aggressive treatment protocol.

steps.tx: Classic radiographic features reflect aggressive cortical breakthrough and periosteal irritation. As the tumor elevates the periosteum, ossification at the acute angle beneath the stripped membrane forms a **Codman triangle**. Concurrently, malignant bone formed along the path of stretched Sharpey fibers produces perpendicular bony spicules, imparting the pathognomonic sunburst appearance on anteroposterior and lateral knee radiographs.
steps.say: On plain radiographs, look for a destructive mixed lytic and sclerotic lesion in the metaphysis. As it bursts through the cortex, it lifts the periosteum to create a Codman triangle at the margins. Spicules of tumor bone growing along stretched Sharpey fibers create the classic sunburst or sunray pattern.

points: Elevation of periosteum by expanding tumor

right.title: Sunburst Reaction
points: New bone along perpendicular Sharpey fibers
Radiates outward into soft tissue mass

steps.tx: Modern multimodal management commences with **neoadjuvant chemotherapy** using multi-agent regimens combining high-dose methotrexate, doxorubicin (adriamycin), and cisplatin (the MAP protocol). Preoperative chemotherapy halts systemic micrometastatic dissemination, shrinks the local soft tissue mass, and facilitates surgical resection. Histological tumor necrosis exceeding ninety percent in the resected specimen indicates a good histological response and predicts long-term survival.
steps.say: Treatment begins with neoadjuvant chemotherapy using high-dose methotrexate, adriamycin, and cisplatin. Preoperative chemotherapy kills microscopic metastases and shrinks the tumor. When the bone is removed, a pathologist assesses necrosis. Tumor necrosis over ninety percent signals an excellent response and translates to superior long-term survival.

steps.tx: Advances in imaging and endoprosthetics enable **limb salvage surgery** in over eighty-five percent of patients today, completely supplanting primary amputation. The surgeon performs a wide en bloc resection of the affected bone with a three-centimeter safe margin, followed by reconstruction using a modular titanium endoprosthesis. Amputation is reserved solely for cases where major neurovascular encasement or severe pathological fractures preclude clean resection.
steps.say: Over eighty-five percent of patients are now candidates for limb salvage surgery rather than amputation. The entire diseased bone segment is removed with clear margins and replaced with a modular titanium mega-prosthesis. Amputation is reserved only for rare cases where major nerves and blood vessels are completely encased.

points: En bloc excision with clear margins
Preserves functional limb and quality of life

right.title: Amputation Indications
points: Complete encasement of major neurovascular bundle

quiz.q: What is the mandatory histopathological feature required to establish the diagnosis of osteosarcoma?
options: Direct production of malignant osteoid by pleomorphic stromal cells
Sheets of small round blue cells with positive CD99 staining
Abundant multinucleated giant cells within a benign vascular stroma
Signet ring cells distended by intracytoplasmic mucin pools
quiz.explain: The pathognomonic histological hallmark of osteosarcoma is the direct synthesis of malignant osteoid (unmineralised bone matrix) by malignant pleomorphic mesenchymal cells.

quiz.q: What percentage of tumor necrosis on the resected specimen defines a good histological response to neoadjuvant chemotherapy?
quiz.explain: According to the Huvos grading system, a necrosis rate of 90% or greater in the resected specimen following neoadjuvant chemotherapy signifies a good histological response and favorable prognosis.
